name: Natural gas; onshore, unconventional; at well
description: This process represents average US natural gas at the Production stage (Production operations for onshore unconventional natural gas production) System boundary: natural gas resource extraction at the well only. Inputs: natural gas resource in the ground, diesel fuel for drilling-adjacent field equipment, electricity, and water. Outputs: 1 m3 of natural gas at the well, plus direct fugitive methane and VOC emissions, combustion emissions (via linked background processes), and flared gas. Does not include any upstream activity — this is the first stage of the supply chain. The source is GREET 2025 Rev1 (Argonne National Laboratory). Two methane leakage methods are available; the default is the BU/TD Hybrid method. To switch to bottom-up only, change the global parameter CH4_LEAKAGE_METHOD from 1 to 2 in openLCA. For more information about the data source and transformations applied to convert GREET outputs to openLCA format, visit https://github.com/FLCAC-admin/FDC-curation-admin/tree/main/GREET_ng.
category: 21: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction/2111: Oil and Gas Extraction

processDocumentation.timeDescription: This process represents the U.S. natural gas supply chain as of 2020, consistent with the base year used in GREET 2025 Rev1 for EPA Greenhouse Gas Inventory methane leakage data. EIA production share data reflect 2024 conditions.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: US natural gas supply chain — Production stage, Onshore Unconventional. Stage energy efficiency: 0.99246 (GREET NG_Regions row 80); feed input = 1.0121 m3 per m3 output (1/efficiency). Direct emissions on this process are fugitive only (CH4 leakage and VOC venting). Combustion and flaring emissions are modeled on linked equipment background processes.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Attributional. End-use and end-of-life stages are excluded.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Lower heating value (LHV): 38.23 MJ/m3 (default; configurable). Energy efficiency per stage from GREET NG_Regions row 80. US production shares: Onshore Conventional 19.1%, Onshore Unconventional 77.9%, Offshore 3.0% (GREET NG_Regions row 11, 2024 EIA data). Methane leakage method: CH4_LEAKAGE_METHOD = 1 (BU/TD Hybrid, default) or 2 (Bottom-Up only). Diesel upstream petroleum refining impacts excluded from system boundary.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Direct combustion emissions are modeled via linked background equipment processes rather than on the stage processes directly — this is an intentional structural choice that keeps background processes independently reusable. Petroleum upstream impacts for diesel combustion are excluded; only direct combustion emission factors from the GREET EF tab are applied, consistent with a wellhead-to-citygate system boundary. Elementary flows contributing less than 1% of total mass flow are excluded. No formal mass balance was calculated; energy efficiency losses are represented by the feed input quantity (1/efficiency m3 per m3 output).
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: All inventory data are sourced directly from GREET 2025 Rev1 (NG_Regions tab), read programmatically at runtime from the source spreadsheet. Energy use values come from rows 92-96; emission factors from rows 104-117; equipment type fractions from rows 22-30 and 89-90. Production shares (onshore conventional 19.1%, onshore unconventional 77.9%, offshore 3.0%) come from row 11, based on 2024 EIA data. Methane leakage rates come from GREET Inputs rows 133-138. The default BU/TD Hybrid method combines EPA GHGI top-down inventory data with bottom-up direct measurements (Burnham et al. 2025, ANL-25/18, Section 3.2).
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: GREET values expressed per mmBtu of NG throughput are converted to SI units per m3 of natural gas output. Unit conversion factors are documented in the flow property descriptions. NG combustion at each stage is split by equipment type using compression and general combustion fractions read directly from GREET rows 89-90, multiplied by global equipment shares from rows 26-30. Storage and Distribution are production-weighted averages across the three production types. Production, gathering and boosting, Processing, and Transmission are provided as separate unit processes per production type.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: System boundary: natural gas resource extraction at the well only. Inputs: natural gas resource in the ground, diesel fuel for drilling-adjacent field equipment, electricity, and water. Outputs: 1 m3 of natural gas at the well, plus direct fugitive methane and VOC emissions, combustion emissions (via linked background processes), and flared gas. Does not include any upstream activity — this is the first stage of the supply chain.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: Situation C1 - Accounting, with system-external interactions - The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analyzed system including existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model. Only criteria air pollutants are included. The target audience of this model includes LCA practitioners, industry, and the general public.

parameters.name: gen_uib_share
parameters.description: Share of general combustion going to utility/industrial boilers. Source: NG_Regions!B29. Value: 0.00000 (global, all stages). Currently 0 — UIB share is zero in GREET 2025 Rev1.

parameters.name: gen_lgt_share
parameters.description: Share of general combustion going to large gas turbines. Source: NG_Regions!B28. Value: 0.50000 (global, all stages).

parameters.name: gen_sib_share
parameters.description: Share of general combustion going to small industrial boilers. Source: NG_Regions!B30. Value: 0.50000 (global, all stages).

parameters.name: ch4_leakage_active
parameters.description: The methane leakage value currently active for this process, selected by the global parameter CH4_LEAKAGE_METHOD. When CH4_LEAKAGE_METHOD = 1, this equals ch4_leakage_hybrid. When CH4_LEAKAGE_METHOD = 2, this equals ch4_leakage_bottom_up. This parameter drives the CH4 exchange amount formula — do not edit this parameter directly. Change CH4_LEAKAGE_METHOD instead to switch all 14 stage processes simultaneously.

parameters.name: ng_combusted_total
parameters.description: Total natural gas combusted at this stage in m3 per m3 NG output. = NG_Regions!H94 ÷ 1,000,000. In m3 because combustion flows use Volume (m3) as their reference unit, keeping the mass balance directly comparable to the natural gas chain flows. Value: 7.40510e-03 m3/m3. Equivalent energy: 2.83100e-01 MJ/m3.

parameters.name: ch4_leakage_bottom_up
parameters.description: Methane leakage rate for this stage using the Bottom-Up only method (CH4_LEAKAGE_METHOD = 2). Based on direct measurement surveys only, without top-down inventory adjustment. Generally produces lower leakage estimates than the hybrid method. Value: 1.63561e-03 kg CH4 per m3 NG output. Source: GREET Inputs tab, Inputs!O133.

parameters.name: comp_frac
parameters.description: Fraction of total NG combusted used in compression equipment. Source: NG_Regions!H90. Value: 0.92408. Applied to reciprocating engine exchange. gen_frac + comp_frac = 1.0.

parameters.name: comp_re_share
parameters.description: Share of compression combustion going to reciprocating engines. Source: NG_Regions!B26. Value: 1.00000 (global, all stages).

parameters.name: gen_frac
parameters.description: Fraction of total NG combusted used in general (non-compression) equipment. Source: NG_Regions!H89. Value: 0.07592. Applied to LGT and SIB exchanges.

parameters.name: ng_flared_total
parameters.description: Total natural gas flared at this stage (m3 per m3 NG output). Source: NG_Regions!H95 ÷ 1,000,000. Value: 3.96680e-04 m3/m3.

parameters.name: ch4_leakage_hybrid
parameters.description: Methane leakage rate for this stage using the BU/TD Hybrid method (GREET default, CH4_LEAKAGE_METHOD = 1). Combines EPA Greenhouse Gas Inventory top-down estimates with bottom-up direct measurements. Value: 2.74860e-03 kg CH4 per m3 NG output. Source: GREET Inputs tab, Inputs!L133.
